draft.title: The spread of world religions
card: Between 600 and 1750 CE, Christianity, Islam and Buddhism spread far beyond where they began. They reached people across Asia, Africa and Europe.
Trade
Merchants carried their faith along trade routes and shared it with the people they met. Islam reached parts of Southeast Asia this way.
Conquest
Armies and rulers brought new lands under their control, and their religion often came with them. Islam spread widely across North Africa and Western Asia after 632 CE.
Missionaries
Missionaries are people who travel to teach their religion. Buddhist monks carried Buddhism along the Silk Roads, and Christian missionaries travelled to many lands.
draft.remember: Religions spread by trade, conquest and missionaries, and they shaped laws and ways of life.

a.q: Which of these is an example of a religion spreading through missionaries?
opts: Monks travel to a distant land to teach Buddhism
Merchants share their faith while selling silk
An army takes a city and its ruler changes religion
A family moves to a nearby town for farm work
a.why: Missionaries are people who travel in order to teach their religion, as the monks did. Merchants spread ideas as a side effect of trade, so that is the spread through trade, not missionaries.
a.clue: Look for people whose main purpose in travelling is to teach.

b.q: In 1100 CE, a merchant sails from Arabia to a port in Southeast Asia. He sells cloth and talks about his Muslim faith with local people, and some of them later convert. How did Islam spread here?
opts: Through trade, as a merchant shared his faith
Through conquest, as an army took the port
Through missionaries, as he travelled to teach
Through law, as a ruler forced everyone to change
b.why: The merchant came to sell cloth and shared his faith while doing so, so this is spread through trade. No army was involved, and his main aim was not teaching, so he was not a missionary.
b.clue: Ask why the man travelled and whether any army was involved.

a.best: Monks travel to a distant land to teach Buddhism

b.best: Through trade, as a merchant shared his faith
